status: CPU compilation and static checks complete; GPU attribution and speed unmeasured

attribution.known: The rejected quantizer adds one CTA barrier site and 70 warp-shuffle sites to the compiled Decode kernel. Scale caching adds three warp-shuffle sites and no CTA barrier site. All four controls compile with zero Decode spills.
attribution.unknown: The previous combined GPU run cannot identify which change dominated the regression, their interaction, or kernel-internal stall reasons. Static instruction sites are not executed instruction counts, latency, or throughput.
attribution.quant_only_scope: The quantizer factor includes register-resident values, revised reduction/packing, a higher math-register budget and the extra barrier; it does not isolate the barrier alone.
attribution.barrier_candidate_scope: The no-extra-barrier candidate retains read-only partial maxima and repeats scale reduction in each warp. Comparing it with quant-only would test that complete replacement, not a pure barrier-latency experiment.
future_contrasts_if_gpu_is_authorized: combined minus quant-only minus scale-only plus baseline
attribution.future_measurement_requirements: Use identical numerical seeds, workloads, batching, routing comparisons and separate unprofiled score/profile windows. Preserve all four controls; do not infer causality from unmatched microbenchmark seeds.

improvements.register-redux: Keep SwiGLU values in registers, publish immutable partial maxima, compute scales in each warp, and use exact eight-lane unsigned REDUX for nonnegative FP32 maxima. Removes inverse-scale scratch reuse and its additional CTA barrier.
improvements.warp-redux-r176: Use a swizzled shared FP32 layout and one warp per group64 row, with exact full-warp REDUX. Increase math-register allocation from 168 to 176 to remove the observed 8-byte store/load spills.
improvements.deprioritized: warp-redux at 168 math registers spills 8 bytes in each direction; retain only as the reproducible predecessor of warp-redux-r176.
improvements.numerical_scope: Retain all group64 values, FP8 E4M3 conversion, SiLU, clamping, the existing scale formula and reciprocal helper. Integer ordering is used only for an exact maximum of nonnegative FP32 magnitudes.
improvements.tradeoffs: REDUX reduces the shuffle tree but introduces collective/control instructions; register-redux repeats scale work. CPU compilation alone cannot rank their speed or establish a 7200-goodput projection.
